Welcome to Beech Lodge
We think differently about children who think differently.
Great Minds Think Differently
Beech Lodge is an award-winning special school offering a transformational and enriching education for pupils aged 7-18. We cater for children & young people with social, emotional and learning difficulties primarily due to developmental trauma and adverse childhood experiences.
Our Approach
Our sensitive and nurturing relationship-based approach is underpinned by a profound understanding of social, emotional and communication difficulties and the impact that early trauma has on a child's school experience. We aim to ensure that all pupils feel a sense of belonging at school and know that their presence here matters to us.
Admissions
We're happy to have a chat about your child's particular needs, however all pupils that join Beech Lodge must have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and all admissions must come via your Local Education Authority.

Our Children
Beech Lodge School is designed for pupils aged 7-18 who have social & emotional difficulties and who may have been exposed to trauma and adverse childhood experiences. Many of our pupils are care-experienced (adopted, previously looked after and looked after children & young people)
Our pupils may also have additional learning difficulties, communication and developmental needs. They may require specialist teaching for specific learning difficulties, as well as access to therapeutic interventions such as Speech and Language, Occupational and Play Therapy.
Our children have a range of challenges including:
Our individually tailored, flexible approach at enables children to thrive rather than just survive at school. We offer an empathic and good humoured environment for children to flourish.
Emotional and social difficulties
Specific learning difficulties including dyslexia and dyscalculia
Developmental trauma and ACE's
ASD, ADHD and sensory processing issues
Executive functioning difficulties
School phobia / anxiety
Missed opportunities at school
PLEASE NOTE
Due to the nature of our school, we are unable to cater for children who require constant individual supervision or who have aggressive, violent or sexualised behaviour.
We fondly refer to a typical Beech Lodge child as a 'sparky square peg' in the round hole of mainstream education. We are proud to give our children the 'empathic square hole' in which to truly fit.

Educational Development & Curriculum
At Beech Lodge School, we focus on the unique nature of every pupil. Our bespoke, engaging and flexible curriculum is tailored to meet pupil needs, interests and academic ability.
Whilst it is based on the national curriculum, it is carefully structured and delivered in a way that works for individuals who respond to an alternative approach to learning and their school environment. A profound understanding of child development means that the social & emotional functioning of every pupil is considered at all times. This takes into account individual learning styles, strengths, and difficulties. We help to navigate their own challenges and reach their personal goals whatever that may look like for them.
The pupils have access to a range of subjects, qualifications and extra-curricular activities which enable them to fulfil their potential and prepare for the next stage of their lives. Pupils are taught in very small classes with a high adult ratio as well as specialist teaching to support pupils with specific learning difficulties.
Inclusivity is at the heart of our educational approach. We work to ensure that pupils feel safe and develop effective relationships to enable access to learning.
The curriculum offers pupils a thorough, fun and practical journey through which they develop a joy of learning and a sense of achievement and pride. We work with each child’s strengths, interests and experiences in order to develop their self-confidence, their ability for self-exploration and improve effectiveness at collaborative working.
Our fundamental aim is to help each child to think independently, to be able to read between the lines, to be curious and question, to see the bigger picture and to make connections with their own lives and the wider world.
The skill-based curriculum is taught in an active rather than passive fashion, using the outdoor environment, cookery, music and discussion to bring subjects to life and make them meaningful to themselves and their future.

Physical and Sensory Development
At Beech Lodge, we recognise the importance of physical and sensory development for our pupils. We have designed our curriculum with this in mind to ensure that it supports the growth & progress of each child.
Many of our pupils have sensory needs and we meet these by providing a holistic sensory-friendly environment that supports their learning and overall wellbeing.
The school buildings and playground and have been designed to be calm and to reduce sensory overload. The classrooms are created to provide an optimal sensory environment and supportive strategies are incorporated into the class routines to address physical and sensory needs while engaging students in learning.
We understand the therapeutic benefits of physical development, engaging with nature and staying active. See Outdoor Education for more detailed information.

There is also our dedicated and qualified Occupational Therapist to advise on sensory and physical development. Where needed, pupils receive direct Occupational Therapy input (individual and/or group). There are further therapeutic services available including play therapy, speech & language therapy and physical therapy, all designed to support sensory and physical development.

Development of Communication skills
Children and young people at Beech Lodge School are supported in all aspects of communication, verbal and non-verbal, throughout the school day.
This is done via explicit teaching, incidental learning and input from our Speech and Language Therapist who runs direct individual and group interventions as well as providing guidance to all staff, which is integrated throughout our approach.
Through this input we support pupils to express their wants and needs, communicate their desires and fears, including putting big feelings into words.

Frequently Asked Questions
We are a relationally focused special school that works utilising the principles of belonging and more significantly mattering to enhance the school experiences of our children. We want our young people to be proud of where they have come from and be aspirational in where they are going regardless of previous experiences or level of additional need. All of our students have EHCP’s and require a different approach to school based learning.
The school focuses on working relationally with every member of the community children. The principles of mattering underpin our day to day existence and this is critical to the social and emotional development of our students. The purpose of this is to try and maximise the success of the placement, not only from an academic perspective but holistically in all aspects of the individuals life. Focusing on the building of accessible independence to the level that is right for the specific child and their family.
No we work relationally across the board and the approach of the school is consistent with all students regardless of diagnosis or other associated status or need. Cohorts are assembled to maximise the potential for individual successes and promote a sense of belonging in all our students. The highest priority is the development of their sense of self worth and cementing a knowledge in them that they have a value to contribute to wider society regardless of their background or range of needs.
Fee packages are bespoke based on the individuals EHCP and provision is mapped and built around the documentation supplied in the initial application. Any amendments are then made through statutory due process.
Yes. All of our pupils have an Education, Health and Care Plan (EHCP) and are placed and funded by their LEA's.
Yes unfortunately due to the complex and trauma based needs of our cohorts we are not suitable for students who present with volatile outwards facing behaviours, who require physical intervention to maintain safety or have sexually harmful or challenging behaviours.

Our ultimate goal is to prepare our children for the next stage in life and to be effective members of society. That may mean a place at college, a return to mainstream education, the workplace or an apprenticeship. Our links with local colleges means many of our pupils go on to study for a further qualifications or apprenticeship.

A welcome from our new Head
Welcome to Beech Lodge,
My name is James Thorpe and I am delighted to be taking over the role of Headteacher from this September.
I arrived at Beech Lodge in Sept 2022, having spent over 20 years working in mainstream secondary schools in a range of roles. When I applied to Beech Lodge, I said that the motto ‘Great Minds Think Differently’ resonated with me and this continues to be true: the last four years have shown how our motto is more than just a strapline, it is ingrained in the DNA of the school. Working in such a forward-thinking and pupil-centred school enables us to identify and implement creative initiatives that truly meet the needs of our exceptional young people. I am proud to be Headteacher of a truly unique school, one which fully embodies a personalised approach and where pupils are supported and challenged in equal measure, allowing them to flourish.
